title: NEW: Dr. Scott W. Harold Named Director of CNAS Indo-Pacific Security Program
gist: CNAS press release naming Dr. Scott W. Harold (ex-RAND, Pentagon East Asia adviser 2022-2024) as director of its Indo-Pacific Security Program, with a mandate on alliances, deterring China and North Korea, and the security effects of transformative technologies.

insights.claim: CNAS appointed Dr. Scott W. Harold, previously a senior political scientist at RAND and from 2022 to 2024 senior advisor to the deputy assistant secretary of defense for East Asia, as senior fellow and director of its Indo-Pacific Security Program.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: A former Pentagon East Asia official leading an influential think-tank program signals continuity in hawkish-alliance Indo-Pacific policy thinking.
insights.locator: Harold joins CNAS from the RAND

insights.claim: CNAS CEO Richard Fontaine framed the program's priorities as strengthening U.S. alliances, deterring China and North Korea, and maintaining stability in what he called the world's most critical region.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Deterrence-of-China focus reinforces the demand-side narrative for Indo-Pacific defense spending.
insights.quote: strengthening U.S. alliances, deterring China and North Korea, and maintaining stability in the world’s most critical region

insights.claim: Harold said the United States and its allies face hard choices as they grapple with transformative technologies and new threats.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Technology (incl. AI) is becoming central to alliance-security agendas.
insights.quote: The United States and its allies face hard choices as they grapple with transformative technologies and new threats.

insights.claim: Recent CNAS Indo-Pacific research covered the effects of AI on the U.S.-China relationship, repairing U.S.-India relations, and securing Taiwan's information security.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Flags policy focus areas — U.S.-India repair and Taiwan info-security — that may shape future policy recommendations.

insights.claim: Harold is fluent in Mandarin and wrote his Columbia PhD dissertation on China's decision-making on joining the World Trade Organization.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Background indicates China political-economy depth in program leadership.
